clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms at the close of Saturday, December 26, 1931, the only day on which it closes the District offices and excuses employees ('be closed on Saturday, December 26, 1931 ... are hereby excused from duty on that day'). Actor: EO 5763 itself. The dossier holds no own-terms record for this order, so the end cites the order's complete held text, which contains the stated day.

research_rationale:
EO 5763 (December 22, 1931, Herbert Hoover), titled 'Christmas, 1931'. Text and identity: the dossier's original is the Office of the Federal Register's 1974 compilation, Proclamations and Executive Orders: Herbert Hoover, vol. II, printed pages 1051-1052 (official_compilation_high, acceptable_as_original true), held as the OCR text layer jobs/ofr-compilations/output/texts/EO_5763.txt, which I read in full. The compilation PDF itself is not materialized in this checkout (releases/source_books holds only a 133-byte pointer), so the printed page images were not viewed and original_pages_confirmed stays false. The OCR is clean; its only defects are stray spaces before commas and in '26 , 1931'. Number, date and subject agree across the compilation heading and closing tag '[No. 5763]', the census register (1931-12-22) and the WPA 1944 list ('ordered closed on Dec. 26, 1931. 1932 CSR 65'). It closes the executive departments and independent establishments in the District of Columbia, including the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and stations, on Saturday, December 26, 1931, and excuses federal employees in the District from duty that day, except those excepted for special public reasons or whose absence would be inconsistent with existing law. The type label office_closing_mourning fits. First end: by its own terms at the close of 1931-12-26, the only day it governs. December 26, 1931 was a Saturday, as the order says. Searches on 2026-10-28: the WPA 1944 list and census titles for Christmas and late-December closings 1931-1936 (EO 5977 of December 19, 1932 and EO 7499 of November 27, 1936 are new orders for other years and do not name EO 5763), and a citation search of every held order text for 'Order No. 5763' (only navigation links in Wikisource pages for adjacent numbers); nothing names EO 5763.
